getting_started_intro: A few steps to set up your household: each leads to the page that does it, and brings you back here.
getting_started_tags_hint: Tags sort where the money goes: start from the suggested ones and uncheck what doesn't concern you.
getting_started_accounts_hint: Import a statement from your bank: it makes the accounts, with their balance and their history. Or add an account by hand.
getting_started_wallet_hint: A cash account: money withdrawn goes there, and counting it records what you spent without noting it.
getting_started_members_hint: The others record their expenses too, and see the household's accounts.
getting_started_imported_hint: Your bank's history, for each account and card: what is already entered is recognized, never counted twice.
getting_started_recurring_hint: Rent, subscriptions, pay: recorded on their day, or waiting for you to check them. Those found in your imported history are suggested.
getting_started_budgets_hint: How much for groceries, outings: the app says where you stand, month by month.
getting_started_categorized_hint: A history imported comes without tags: sort it by payee, all of a payee's transactions at once. The next imports learn from it.
categorize_intro: Your expenses and incomes without a tag, by payee, the most frequent first. Choose a tag: all of the payee's take it, and the next imports will suggest it.
categorize_empty: Nothing left to sort: every expense and income of your accounts has a tag.
categorize_suggest_intro: The assistant can suggest one of your tags for each payee, 50 at a time. Nothing is applied until you choose to.
categorize_no_suggestion: No suggestion: choose a tag yourself.
categorize_apply_all_text: Payees: {payees}. Transactions that will take the tag shown: {count}. You can change a transaction's tag afterwards.
help_account_visibility_text: What the other members see of this account: its details (every transaction) or its balance only. Its amounts always count in the household's totals and reports; its holders always see everything.
help_account_holders_text: The members whose account it is: only they record its transactions or change it. With several holders, it is a joint account.
help_opening_balance_text: What the account held before the first transaction recorded in it. Made from a statement, it is the bank's, and follows the history when you import further back.
help_amount_owed_text: For a card or a loan, what you owe on it, as a positive amount: the app keeps it as a negative balance, a debt, counted in the household's liabilities.
help_consolidated_view_text: Every account of the household together, computed each time: the assets (what the accounts hold), the liabilities (what cards and loans owe) and the net balance, one less the other. Transfers between accounts change nothing in it.
help_transfer_text: An expense or an income is money leaving or entering the household. Money moving between two of its accounts (cash taken out to your wallet, a card's payment) is a transfer: it never counts in the reports.
help_lines_text: A transaction can be split into lines, each with its amount and at most one tag: groceries and household items on one receipt, say. A line without a tag shows as uncategorized; reports count each amount once.
help_adjust_balance_text: It brings the account to what it really holds (the cash counted, the bank's balance): the gap is recorded on that day as an adjustment, an expense when it holds less, an income when it holds more.
help_recurring_mode_text: Recorded automatically: the transaction is made on its day, as it is. To check: on its day, it waits on your dashboard for you to confirm it, its amount changed if needed, or to skip it; importing a statement can confirm it too.
help_budget_period_text: A monthly budget starts again each month; a yearly one counts the whole year, for what comes back seldom (insurance, gifts). What its tag's sub-tags spend counts in it.
help_import_known_text: A line is already entered when a transaction of the account has the same amount, from 5 days before to 3 days after: it is tied to it, never recorded twice. A transfer's other side entered in another account becomes the transfer. A line imported once is never imported again.
help_import_file_text: It is read to show you its lines, then forgotten: never kept. Of an account's number, only a key is kept, to recognize the account next time, with its last digits.
help_sharing_split_text: How a shared expense is divided at first, by weights: 1 and 1 halves it, 2 and 1 gives two thirds to the first. Each expense can be split otherwise.
help_intro: How Grand Livre works, section by section, then the questions asked often.
help_faq_none: No question matches: try other words.
help_section_getting_started_p1: A household is the people who share their money. Each member signs in with their own email; the household's owners invite the others and manage its members.
help_section_getting_started_p2: When a household starts, Getting started lists the steps in order: tags, accounts (best from a bank statement), a wallet, the other members, the history imported then sorted, recurring transactions and budgets. It stays on the dashboard until done, and on the household's page.
help_section_getting_started_p3: You can belong to several households: the household's name, at the top, lists yours and switches from one to the other, on each device. It also shows the invitations you received, and creates or joins another household.
help_section_accounts_p1: Each account has a type and one or more holders: only its holders record its transactions. Its visibility says what the other members see of it: its details, or its balance only. Its amounts always count in the household's balance.
help_section_accounts_p2: Cards and loans are debts: enter what you owe, the app keeps it as a negative balance. The household's balance adds everything up: the assets, the liabilities, and the net balance.
help_section_accounts_p3: A wallet is a cash account: taking cash out is a transfer to it, and counting it records what you spent without noting it. Any account can be brought to its bank's balance the same way.
help_section_accounts_p4: An account with transactions can't be deleted: archive it. It keeps its history, and its balance still counts.
help_section_transactions_p1: An expense or an income is money leaving or entering the household. Money moving between two of its accounts is a transfer: it never counts as an expense or an income.
help_section_transactions_p2: A transaction can be split into lines, each with its amount and at most one tag; a line without a tag is uncategorized. Any holder of an account records and changes its transactions, whoever entered them.
help_section_transactions_p3: Tags are the household's, shared by its members, and can sit under one another ("Car › Insurance"): reports add a tag's sub-tags to it. A tag can have a name in each language; without one, it shows another language's. A tag with sub-tags or transactions can't be deleted.
help_section_quick_entry_p1: Type a note ("groceries at Costco 82.40 yesterday"), or dictate it with the microphone: your voice is transcribed by Mistral, then deleted, and you read the text before sending it. The assistant makes a draft, which you check before it is saved. Nothing is saved without you.
help_section_quick_entry_p2: Photograph a receipt: before it is sent, you can turn it, crop it, zoom in and mask what shouldn't leave your device. Only the photo prepared is sent, then dropped: never stored. What was read on it (merchant, date, total, items) is kept with the transaction.
help_section_quick_entry_p3: The assistant only receives what you may see: the note or the photo, your accounts, the tags and recent payees.
help_section_imports_p1: Export the CSV file of your bank (Desjardins for now: accounts and cards) and choose it: it is read, compared with what is in the app, then forgotten. Nothing is imported before you check each line.
help_section_imports_p2: Each account of the file goes to one of your accounts, or to a new one made from the statement with its balance; a card replaced under a new number can join the same account. Lines already entered, recurring days waiting and transfers entered on the other account are recognized: nothing is counted twice.
help_section_imports_p3: An import is all or nothing. Whoever made it can undo it from the import page: what it recorded is deleted, what it tied to your entries stays.
help_section_sorting_p1: A history imported comes without tags. Sort it by payee: one tag for all of a payee's transactions at once, its refunds apart. The next imports suggest the tag a payee had.
help_section_sorting_p2: The page opens from Transactions ("Sort by payee") while payees are left. "Suggest tags" asks the assistant for one of your tags per payee, 50 at a time: it gets each payee with its number of transactions and usual amount, your tags, and the payees already tagged. Each suggestion is marked and changes as you wish; nothing is applied until you sort a payee, or apply every tag shown at once after a confirmation.
help_section_recurring_p1: Rent, subscriptions, pay: a recurring transaction comes back every week, month or year from its first day, until an end day if it has one. The dashboard shows the next ones.
help_section_recurring_p2: Recorded automatically, it is made on its day as it is. To check, it waits on the dashboard for you to confirm it (its amount changed if needed) or skip it; importing a statement can confirm it too.
help_section_recurring_p3: What comes back on a regular schedule in the accounts you hold (a mortgage, a pay, a bill) is spotted in your history and suggested below the list, with how often it was seen and its amounts. "Make it recurring" opens the form filled in, to check; "Not recurring" stops suggesting it, to every member.
help_section_budgets_p1: A budget says how much for a tag, monthly or yearly, from a month on; what its sub-tags spend counts in it. The budgets page and the dashboard say where each stands, in words: under, near, over.
help_section_reports_p1: The expenses and incomes of a period, tag by tag: each tag with its sub-tags added, its refunds taken off; transfers never count. The trend shows the twelve months ending with the period.
help_section_sharing_p1: Off by default, for the households that settle between members. Once an owner turns it on in the household's settings, an expense paid from a personal account can be split among members; the sharing page says who owes whom, and the fewest payments to settle.
help_section_app_p1: Install Grand Livre from your browser ("Add to Home Screen", or the account menu's "Install the app"): it opens like an app. What the other members change shows at once, without reloading.
faq_visibility_q: Can the other members see all my transactions?
faq_visibility_a: Only if your account shows its details. Set its visibility to its balance only: they see its balance, its transactions stay yours. Its amounts still count in the household's totals.
faq_cash_q: I took cash out: is it an expense?
faq_cash_a: No: a transfer from your account to your wallet. What you then spend in cash is an expense from the wallet; counting your wallet records what you didn't note.
faq_card_q: Why is my card's balance negative?
faq_card_a: A card owes money: its balance is that debt, negative. Paying the card from your account is a transfer, not an expense: the expenses are the purchases made with it.
faq_import_twice_q: If I import the same statement twice, is it counted twice?
faq_import_twice_a: No: each line keeps an identity, the same in every export, and a line already imported into an account is never imported again.
faq_entered_then_imported_q: I entered an expense by hand, then imported the statement: is it twice?
faq_entered_then_imported_a: No, when it is the same amount within a few days: the import ties the bank's line to your entry rather than recording it again. Your entry stays as you wrote it.
faq_receipt_kept_a: No. It is sent to the assistant to be read, then dropped. Only what was read is kept, and you can mask what you don't want to send before it leaves.
faq_file_kept_q: Is my bank file, or my account's number, kept?
faq_file_kept_a: No. The file is forgotten once read. Of the account's number, only a key is kept, to recognize the account next time, with its last digits.
faq_undo_import_q: How do I undo an import?
faq_undo_import_a: On the import page, under your recent imports: Undo. What it recorded is deleted, even if you changed it since; what it tied to your entries stays as it was.
faq_delete_q: Why can't I delete this account, or this tag?
faq_delete_a: So no history is lost: an account with transactions is archived instead; a tag with sub-tags or transactions must be emptied first.
faq_currency_q: How do I change the household's currency?
faq_currency_a: In the household's settings, as long as it has no account: once an account exists, the currency stays.
faq_households_q: Can I belong to several households?
faq_households_a: Yes: accept the invitation of each, or create another one with "Create or join a household" under the household's name, at the top. Choose there the one you work on; each device remembers its own.
faq_language_q: Can I use the app in another language?
faq_language_a: Yes: English, French or Spanish, from the language menu at the top. Each member chooses theirs, and a tag can have a name in each language.
voice_denied: The microphone is blocked: allow it for this site in your browser, or type the note.
voice_failed: The microphone couldn't record: type the note.

error_voice_unavailable: Dictation is unavailable for now: type the note.
faq_voice_a: No. The recording is sent to Mistral to be turned into text, then deleted; you read the text before it becomes a note. A minute at most.
help_quick_entry_text: Type a note, or dictate it with the microphone: your voice is transcribed by Mistral, then deleted (a minute at most), and you read the text before sending it. The assistant prepares the transaction; you check it before it is saved.
help_receipt_scan_label: How does scanning a receipt work?
help_receipt_scan_text: Take a photo of a receipt, or choose one. Before it is sent, you can turn it, crop it and mask what shouldn't leave your device. The assistant prepares the expense, tag by tag; the photo is never kept.
